subject: GDPR: Transfer Impact / DPA next steps for Order Form
messages:
From: Claire Mitchell <claire.mitchell@acmehealth.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmehealth.com>, simon.gray@sg-legal.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Initial DPA/Transfer questions for Order Form

Hi Olga —

Thanks for the Order Form draft. Before we loop procurement formally we need to confirm a couple of privacy items so I can clear legal. Quick list: 
- DPA: we need your proposed DPA attached to the OF, or confirmation you accept our standard DPA.
- SCCs/TIA: given EU patient data, we require confirmation of the transfer mechanism if processing occurs in the US (SCCs + Transfer Impact Assessment or alternate).
- Roles: confirm whether Redwood will be "Processor" or "Controller" for telemetry and customer data.
- Subprocessors: can you provide an initial list and your subprocessors process for notification/approval?

I attached the Order Form they shared for reference. Can Redwood share the DPA and a short note on transfer risk? Simon from our outside counsel is cc'd for any legal redline questions.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to complete by end of month.

Best,
Claire Mitchell
Head of Data Privacy, Acme Health

Attachment: Acme_AF_OrderForm_v3.pdf

From: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
To: Claire Mitchell <claire.mitchell@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 13:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Initial DPA/Transfer questions for Order Form

Claire —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front: Redwood will act as Processor for customer content and as Controller only for limited telemetry needed to operate the platform (we'll outline both in the DPA). We accept SCCs; we plan to provide either (a) the latest EU Commission SCCs executed via addendum + a short Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA), or (b) an approved EU-based dedicated instance if required by the contract (we can discuss costs).

I've looped in Karthik (legal) and Marissa (account lead). Karthik — can you review our standard DPA and propose any required redlines for Acme? I attached our in-progress redlines and a one-page SCCs summary to speed review.

Next steps proposal:
- Karthik to share redline comments by EOD Wed (16 Jun)
- If S&G wants to propose changes, we can review and aim for a single joint redline exchange.
- If transfers require mitigation beyond SCCs/TIA, we'll surface options (EU region hosting / contract controls).

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_v1_redlines.docx; SCCs_Summary.pdf

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com
To: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Cc: Claire Mitchell <claire.mitchell@acmehealth.com>, simon.gray@sg-legal.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2026 09:38:00 +0000
Subject: Redwood DPA redlines + transfer impact notes

Team / Claire / Simon —

I reviewed Redwood_DPA_v1_redlines.docx and added comments keyed to Acme's asks. High-level points:
1) Roles & scope: confirm Processor for customer content; Controller for platform telemetry. Clause references updated (see §1.1-1.3).
2) SCCs: we will adopt the EU Commission SCCs as Module 2 (processor-to-controller) where applicable and attach them as an exhibit. We note a couple of non-standard commercial clauses (liability cap interplay) that Acme should be aware of when signing SCCs into the OF.
3) Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA): included a short TIA summary (see comment on p.3) — evaluates legal landscape, technical controls (encryption at rest/in transit, access controls, US law risk). Recommendation: include contractual mitigations + technical measures, not rely solely on legal argument.
4) Subprocessors: propose 30-day notice for new subprocessors and an opt-out for prohibited subprocessors tied to high-risk data.
5) Data retention & deletion: clarified retention windows and a defined delete-on-termination procedure with certification within 30 days.
6) Audit & breach notification: 72-hour notification target for security incidents plus SOC 2 report sharing quarterly on request.

Open items for negotiation:
- Contractual carve-outs for law enforcement requests (we mark standard language).
- Specific insurance / liability caps tied to data breaches — Acme requested higher caps; we flagged commercial approval required.

I've attached an exported redline and added inline comments where we need external counsel input. If Simon can send any targeted edits, we can prepare a clean OF+DPA for signature.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v1_redlines.docx (redline export)

From: Simon Gray (S&G Legal) <simon.gray@sg-legal.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
Cc: Claire Mitchell <claire.mitchell@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 11:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redlines + transfer impact notes

Karthik / Olga —

Thanks for the quick review. A couple of points from our side after reading your notes: 
- SCCs: we broadly accept the approach of incorporating the Commission SCCs. We will send two targeted commercial edits: (i) a clarification that where Acme is the data exporter, the SCCs remain the governing transfer mechanism; (ii) a fallback for EU-hosted option if TIA cannot reasonably mitigate US law risk.
- TIA: Simon: can Redwood provide the TIA appendix with technical controls and the location(s) of processing? We need this for internal privacy board sign-off.
- Subprocessors & notice: 30 days is acceptable; we'd prefer an opportunity to object within 10 business days for high-risk subprocessors.

We will prepare a one-page markup (DocuSign template) for commercial edits and circulate via procurement. If Redwood can produce a clean OF+DPA with your redlines applied we can move to signatures rapidly.

Regards,
Simon Gray
Partner, S&G Legal

From: olga_petrov@redwood.example.com
To: Claire Mitchell <claire.mitchell@acmehealth.com>, simon.gray@sg-legal.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.example.com, marissa_cole@redwood.example.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2026 16:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA redlines + transfer impact notes — next steps

Thanks all — quick summary and actions:
- Karthik will produce a clean OF+DPA (redlines applied) + an appendix TIA with processing locations and technical controls by COB Friday (18 Jun).
- Simon / Acme: please send the two small commercial edits and procurement's DocuSign template; Marissa will coordinate signature sequencing.
- On subprocessors: Redwood accepts 30-day notice and will add a 10-business-day objection window for high-risk subprocessors.
- If the TIA flags residual high legal risk for US-hosted processing, we'll propose (a) EU-hosted instance pricing or (b) additional contractual mitigations — we aim to surface costs in the next exchange.

I'll post the clean package to the HubSpot deal and include the DocuSign link when ready.

Olga
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Related HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/ACM-2026-INV-11
DocuSign template link (to follow)
